title: Climate Change and Its Impact on Peace and Security in Southeast Asia
organization: Centre for Non-Traditional Security Studies, S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, Nanyang Technological University
temporal_coverage: Indonesia passages describe 2015 wildfire, 2019 floods, 2022 flooding, and 2023 extreme cold and drought; regional report published November 2023.
methodology: Independent regional study commissioned with UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs support; Indonesia case passages cite agency records and published sources.
limitations: Papua incident counts are historical and citation-based; the report explicitly says weather events did not cause internal conflicts.

title: Social Dimensions of Climate Change in Indonesia: Executive Summary
temporal_coverage: World Bank report disclosed in November 2023; discusses expected climate impacts and prospective coal-transition distributional risks.
methodology: Eight-page executive summary of World Bank analysis of climate impacts, vulnerable groups, and local responses.
limitations: Executive summary only; transition effects are prospective, not observed conflict.

title: Climate Risk and Community Resilience in Indonesia
organization: United Nations Development Programme Indonesia, UNDP Bangkok Regional Hub, and Coordinating Ministry for Human Development and Cultural Affairs
temporal_coverage: Mixed-methods study published October 2025; the publisher summary does not specify fieldwork dates.
methodology: UNDP publication page describes mixed quantitative analysis and qualitative input from communities, stakeholders, and experts.
limitations: Only the directly opened publisher summary was read; its linked 19.9 MB report PDF exceeded browser extraction limits, so no detailed event or village claims are made.

title: Leveraging Community-Driven Development Platforms for Resilience: Lessons from a Global Knowledge Exchange in Jakarta
temporal_coverage: World Bank brief published April 2026; West Java restoration described as beginning about a decade earlier.
methodology: World Bank brief reports field-visit examples and national community-driven climate investment systems discussed at a January 2026 exchange.
limitations: Institutional descriptive brief, not an independent impact evaluation; the West Java restoration location is not named and reported results are not causal estimates.
